findings.title: Preimages: in Russian on desktop the callout sits inside the lit Y pane and hides the disc the Try it asks the user to hover
findings.detail: At 1024, 1152 and 1440 px in Russian (mouse and touch, light and dark), basics/preimages places the callout in the top of the lit Y pane. It covers 68-71 % of the pane, including the pane title and most of the image disc. The Try it says 'hover a point inside the disc, then outside'. In English the shorter callout passes the 12 % rule of step 2b and goes under the pane; the Russian one (329 px tall) does not, so step 3 ('inset', inside the hole) wins. A place along the bottom edge would cover only about 50 px of the pane bottom. The audit does not measure how much of a lit area the callout covers, so this passes.
findings.evidence: Audit rows vfy-3/vfy-4: 1440-light-ru-mouse card [800,60,1120,389] vs Y hole [706,44,1136,612]; 1024-*-ru-* card [634,60,954,389] vs [618,44,972,480], overlap 105280 px2 (68 %); 1152-*-ru-* the same. EN at the same sizes: card at the bottom edge, overlap 6400 px2 (20 px strip). Screenshots work/xvt/test/vfp_cdp/shots/vf/p12-1440ru-preimages.png, p10-1024ru-basics-preimages.png.
findings.fix: In place(), before 'inset', try the edge positions with the least lit area covered (raise the 12 % cap or compare coverage with the inset candidate), and never place inside a hole that holds the Try it's target. Audit: record the callout's overlap with each hole and fail above about 15 % of a hole (or any overlap with the anchor itself on desktop sizes).

findings.owner: engine (or content: a before action) and audit
findings.title: Inverses step with a mouse: the lit f^-1 button is invisible (opacity 0), so the ring surrounds an empty square
findings.detail: branches/inverse lights invBtn, the f^-1 button in '.card .acts'. page.html makes .acts opacity 0 unless the card is hovered or has focus (lines 727-729; visible on touch through @media (hover: none)). The geometry is exact (0 px), but the user sees a ring around nothing at every desktop width, in both languages and themes. Not a regression (v15-base anchors it the same way), but it breaks 'highlights exactly the right area' in what the user sees. visible() and the audit's vis() both call checkVisibility with checkOpacity: false, so neither notices.
findings.evidence: 1440 dark EN: invBtn [684,605.5,708,629.5], computed opacity 1 but ancestor .acts opacity 0; zoom work/xvt/test/vfp_cdp/shots/vf/p7-zoom-branches-inverse.png (empty square), full view p8-1440-inverse.png. Also 1024 RU mouse and 360 RU mouse (opacity product 0). 768 RU touch: visible.
findings.fix: Engine: while a step lights an element whose ancestors multiply to opacity < 0.5, reveal it for the step (for example a data attribute on the nearest .card that the tour CSS maps to '.acts { opacity: 1 }', or an inline opacity on the transparent ancestor, restored on step change), or treat it as not visible and use the next anchor name ('chain'). Content (v15): a before action that focuses the card. Audit: fail when the lit target's ancestor opacity product is below 0.5.

findings.title: On short viewports the callout covers a quarter to a half of the lit area on many steps
findings.detail: At 720x450 (200 % of 1440x900) and 844x390 the callout overlaps the lit area on most steps: deform/transport up to 46 % of the lit pane, basics/preimages 46 %, analysis/targets 46 %, views/patterns 46 % (RU), basics/chain 40 %, analysis/guarantees 39 %, basics/shapes 38 %, analysis/integral 31 %. At 720 RU basics/draw it covers the first third of the bottom tools strip. At 360 x 780 mouse RU views/patterns the sheet covers the last row of swatches. Some overlap is unavoidable here, but nothing measures it and nothing tries to reduce it (for example a shorter callout with the text collapsed).
findings.evidence: Computed from the audit rows (card vs holes): work/xvt/test/vf1_cdp/audit/vfy-1.json (720), vf2 (844). Screenshot work/xvt/test/vfp_cdp/shots/vf/p10-360ru-views-patterns.png.
findings.fix: Measure the overlap in the audit (see V-1). On short viewports prefer the placement that covers the least of the anchor itself, or offer a collapsed callout (title and buttons, text on demand).
